## Overall Goal of the Course

The course covers a wide range of interactions between the environment and socio-economic
development. Students are introduced to various methods for analyzing economic impacts on the
environment, the importance of the environment for economic activities, and the role of social
institutions within the context of economy–environment relationships. In this setting, students
learn about different policy tools that can address (undesired) external effects of economic
activities on the environment and how to evaluate the effectiveness of environmental regulations
from an economic perspective. Over the semester, students work on one particular country or region
case study, which they present as a poster during a poster conference at the end of the semester.

## Learning Goals

Upon completion of this seminar, you will be able to:

**Expertise:**

- Understand the core concepts and analytical perspective of ecological economics
- Explain how different notions of 'economic development' relate to the question of ecological sustainability
- Discuss the relevance of trade-offs between social and environmental goals
- Understand how economic activities and the resulting ecological stressors are globally interrelated

**Methodological Competence:**

- Work with data on socio-economic development and environmental pressures
- Account for environmental stressors at the global level, distinguishing production- and consumption-based perspectives
- Evaluate environmental policy instruments and their underlying assumptions

**Social and Personal Skills:**

- Conduct and present a country-level analysis as part of a group
- Be able to delineate the assumptions on which your own assessments, and those on others depend when it comes to the discussion of social and environmental challenges
- Take well-founded positions in current debates (e.g. growth vs. degrowth)

## Course Information

### Prerequisites
There are no formal prerequisites. A basic familiarity with introductory economics is
helpful but not required. The course is offered jointly for the MA "Sustainable Energy"
and the MA "International Management Studies" programs.

### Course Details

- **Lecture Time:** Wednesdays, 08:30–12:00 (we start 8:30 sharp)
- **Lecturers:** Claudius Gräbner-Radkowitsch & Anna-Katharina Kothe
- **Credits:** 5 ECTS (≈ 150 h total workload; about 7 h of self-study per week on top of the weekly lecture)

### Course Resources

- **Moodle Room:** [room 17919](https://elearning.uni-flensburg.de/moodle/course/view.php?id=17919)
- Passwort will be distributed during the first lecture

## Evaluation and Assessment

The final mark for the course depends on a group **country-analysis poster** and the students'
performance during the final poster presentation. The posters are prepared in groups of up to 3
people and pitched during the poster conference at the end of the semester.

Full details on the poster — the content and guiding questions as well as the examination
criteria and assessment dimensions — are on the dedicated **[examination page](examination.qmd)**.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Study Recommendations
I strongly recommend that you spread your study time fairly evenly throughout the semester. It will save you time and effort if you study and practice constantly.
:::
